summary: The US and China extended their October 2025 trade truce in late September 2026, and China delayed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. Tariffs are still high: about 36.5% on Chinese goods into the US and 31% on US goods into China, per a July 2026 Congressional Research Service report. On Oct 8 the central bank said it will not weaken the yuan to win trade, ahead of EU trade talks. Chinese large caps are weak, with the Shanghai 50 at a 14 month low. US companies that sell a lot in China or depend on Chinese rare earths move on every truce headline.

watch.name: Yuan per US dollar
watch.why: The last close found was about 6.71 in early September, near a three and a half year high for the yuan.

watch.name: Shanghai Composite
watch.why: Down about 3% over the past month; the Shanghai 50 hit a 14 month low.

watch.name: US tariff on Chinese goods
watch.why: Average rate per CRS. Any change in the truce moves it.

watch.name: Rare earth export ban delay ends
watch.why: If China lets the delay lapse, US magnet, defense and car supply chains get squeezed.

exposed.name: Alibaba
exposed.exposure: most revenue from China (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: Moves with Chinese consumer demand, stimulus and US-China tension.

exposed.name: PDD Holdings
exposed.exposure: Pinduoduo in China plus Temu selling Chinese goods abroad (company filings)
exposed.how: Temu is directly hit by US tariffs and duty rules on Chinese goods; the truce extension helps.

exposed.name: JD.com
exposed.exposure: nearly all revenue from China (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: A pure play on Chinese shoppers and stimulus.

exposed.name: Baidu
exposed.exposure: nearly all revenue from China (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: Ad spending in China and US chip export rules for its AI work.

exposed.name: Yum China
exposed.how: Runs KFC and Pizza Hut in China, so it tracks Chinese consumer spending.

exposed.name: Apple
exposed.exposure: about 17% of FY2024 sales from Greater China, and most iPhones are assembled there (FY2024 10-K, approximate)
exposed.how: Hit two ways: Chinese sales and a supply chain that runs through China. The truce extension lowers near term risk.

exposed.name: Qualcomm
exposed.exposure: about 46% of FY2024 revenue billed to China customers (FY2024 10-K, approximate)
exposed.how: Chinese phone makers are its biggest buyers, so trade or export curbs land hard.

exposed.name: Nvidia
exposed.exposure: about 13% of FY2025 revenue from China including Hong Kong (FY2025 10-K, approximate)
exposed.how: US export rules decide which chips it can sell to China.

exposed.name: MP Materials
exposed.exposure: US rare earth producer; China added it to an export control list in June 2026
exposed.how: Gains when China threatens rare earth curbs, since buyers look for non-Chinese supply.

changes.what: The US and China agreed to extend the October 2025 truce, and China pushed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. That lowers near term risk for US firms that sell in China or buy Chinese magnets.
The People's Bank of China said it will not weaken the yuan to gain a trade edge and will publish more currency data from 2027, ahead of EU trade talks.
